name: Derrick Henry

background.fact: Born January 4, 1994 in Yulee, Florida; raised mainly by his grandmother Gladys, who nicknamed him Shocka.

At Yulee High School he set the national high school career rushing yards record; he was a five star recruit and played at Alabama, winning the 2015 Heisman Trophy, Doak Walker Award, Maxwell Award and Walter Camp Award.

Tennessee drafted him in the second round (pick 45) in 2016; he led the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns in 2019 and 2020, ran for over 2,000 yards in 2020 and won the AP Offensive Player of the Year award.
He signed with Baltimore in 2024 and is the NFL active leader in career rushing yards and touchdowns.
Listed at 6 ft 2 in, 252 lb, age 32, jersey 22, in his 11th NFL season; Madden week 8 rating is 96 overall.
Career regular season totals through 2026 week 9: 161 games, 2,837 carries, 13,707 rushing yards, 130 rushing touchdowns.

family.fact: He has been in a relationship with Adrianna Rivas since 2016; they have three daughters. Nothing further about the children is recorded here.
In 2018 he kept a promise to his late grandmother by earning his Alabama degree in communications, and in 2019 he founded the Two All Foundation for young people.

recent_events.fact: Baltimore is 4-5 after four straight losses. The Ravens lost 33-10 at Jacksonville in Week 9, with Joe Fagnano at quarterback; Henry had 17 carries for 57 yards and no catches.
Henry has 689 rushing yards and 8 rushing touchdowns on 175 carries in 9 games, a career low 3.9 yards per carry, and has been held under 100 rushing yards in four straight games.

recent_events.fact: Average is 14.25 fantasy points a game under league scoring; best game was Week 1 vs Indianapolis (144 yards, 3 touchdowns, 34.3 points); since Week 6 he has scored 4.0, 4.9, 12.0 and 5.6.
His snap share has slipped from 54 to 67 percent early in the year to 45 to 51 percent in the last four games; Justice Hill has 33 carries to Henry's 175.

Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) are out; Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett, who is set to start Monday night. Four different quarterbacks have thrown for the Ravens this year (Jackson, Huntley, Fagnano, Brissett next).

reasons: He is active and has 79 percent of Baltimore's carries, so volume is steady even when the team struggles.
Baltimore is a 4.5 point home favorite over a reported 0-8 team, a good game script for a heavy run game.
The implied Ravens total is only 21.5 and Henry has scored under 13 points in four straight games, with 3.9 yards per carry.
Brissett as a new starting quarterback may help the offense; this is untested. A SI start/sit piece says he scored under six points in three of his last four games.

scouts_read: Henry is healthy and still the clear lead back, but the offense around him has fallen apart, with a fourth quarterback now starting. The Ravens are favored by 4.5 at home against a reported winless Chargers team, which should mean a lead and plenty of carries. The problem is efficiency: he is at 3.9 yards per carry, has been under 100 yards for four games, and his snap share has dipped below 50 percent lately. A real quarterback in Brissett could help, and he always has touchdown chances near the goal line. I would project a middling day around 12 to 15 points with a small chance of a big game.
